places.name: Andalen Plantation

why.founding: Andalen Plantation was a House Dres saltrice enterprise. It had a great house, a drying floor, a counting room and a labour row. It was abandoned at the secession. The workers stopped work. The owning family never came back.

why.occupantsMotive: The house stands unoccupied. People from the labour rows down the road work the fields. They take the crop off the land and stop at the drying floor.
why.pressures: The house is intact and unlooted after two centuries. Unnamed hands keep that arrangement in place. The field-holder says House Dres sees to it, but that claim cannot be true.
why.wouldChangeIf: The house would be occupied once the field-holders decided the taboo was over. The house is worth more than the whole village.

places.name: Breathes-Underneath

why.founding: Breathes-Underneath is a chamber under the Loriasel shelf. Air is trapped in its crown. The way in is a slot in the rock. The slot is a sump for two months a year and a squeeze for the rest of the year. It opens on an empty air chamber.

why.occupantsMotive: The divers who use the landing know about the chamber. The divers treat it as a test and not as a resource.
why.pressures: The slot floods in the monsoon. The divers argue about how long the crown's air lasts. Two people have tested it and one came back.

places.name: Buried Blades

why.founding: In 1E 2836 the Argonians stopped fighting the Blackwater War overnight. In the north they buried the proof. A whole district's weapons were oiled, wrapped and put in one pit. Stopping the war could then not easily be undone.
why.siteAdvantages: The pit lies in a dry gravel lens under a low rise. It was chosen because the gravel drains. That is why the contents are still recognisable.
why.occupantsMotive: No guard stands over the pit. Four villages have known where it is for sixteen hundred years. Children are told about the pit as they are told about the deep channel.
why.pressures: An-Xileel interest in the province's armament has made the pit awkward. One of the four villages has started asking what the other three would do.
why.wouldChangeIf: Opening the pit would change the north's politics in a week. It has stayed shut for sixteen centuries.

places.name: Draws-The-Herds

why.founding: When the northern plain under the rim dries, every animal walks to the same three tree-islands for water. For two months this ground holds more wild animals than anywhere else in the region. Predators and hunters follow the herds.
why.siteAdvantages: Three spring-fed pools hold the last standing water on the plain. The pools lie under tree cover at the foot of the rim. They do not fail in a normal dry year.
why.occupantsMotive: Four villages hunt the ground under an allocation. They renegotiate the allocation every year at Wolk Market. The four villages settle their other disputes in the same week.

why.occupantsMotive: Trial marshals and stewards administer the trials and do not defend the town. The Zaht stones of Hist amber do the defending. The Hist has not made a new Zaht stone in four hundred years.

why.wouldChangeIf: The An-Xileel could declare the trials invalid. The province's only route back to a Hist would then close. Every Hist-less settlement in the north would have nowhere to send its own.

why.founding: Hutan-Tzel is an old tribal village on the Panther River. It stands where the river drains into its basin. It holds the western approach to the north. It has its own tribe and its own elder naheesh. The xanmeer Xal Irasotl stands close enough to be the tribe's charge.

why.occupantsMotive: The tribe stays because the Hist speaks here. The totem line is the tribe's to keep. The tribe has dealt carefully with outsiders since the 2E. Few interior tribes deal with outsiders at all.
why.pressures: Tampering with the rune-carved totems attracts dangerous things. Outsiders tamper with the totems. The tribe has a 3E rivalry with Glenbridge across the fringe. In bad years the rivalry costs the tribe a season's trade. The tribe takes in Su-Zahleel survivors who fled the Xit-Xaht. It takes them in without making them kin.
why.wouldChangeIf: The village would close to outsiders entirely. That would follow the first meddled totem that killed a villager. The western approach would close with it.

why.siteAdvantages: The ground is firm where three approaches converge. There is water enough for a market. The roads on either side flood and the town does not.
why.occupantsMotive: The town takes a cut of everything passing between the interior, the border city and the smugglers' port.
why.pressures: The town is prosperous and indefensible. It stands next door to a Daedric ruin, which its people refuse to discuss.
why.wouldChangeIf: The town would be fought over once any of the three roads mattered militarily.

places.name: Fish Boon Ground

why.founding: Hissmir's Fish Boon Feast needs a place to happen. The pilgrimage xanmeer is not that place. This tidal flat below the village has hosted the feast since it began.
why.siteAdvantages: The site is a wide gravel flat where the tide slows. The water is shallow enough for netting from the bank. The flat is wide enough for the whole village and its pilgrims. Every flood scours the flat clean.
why.occupantsMotive: The flat is empty outside the feast. It carries no buildings. The flood scours it every year. The village expects the yearly scouring.
why.pressures: Pilgrim numbers have grown past what the flat can feed. The Root Stewards may not turn a comer away. The feast now runs three days where it once ran one.
why.wouldChangeIf: The feast ground would move upstream if the channel shifted. The channel shifts about once a century. The last shift was in 4E 79.

sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: serves a settlement cluster
hardConstraints: a gravel flat on slow water below Hissmir
annually flooded

netter who says the fish run is smaller every year

vibe.approach: The pilgrim path comes down onto the flat. The whole feast lies laid out below the path.
vibe.senses: Out of season only the tidal water is heard. In season fires burn and fish are gutted at speed. In season there is a great deal of talking.

questHooks.opportunity: The Fish Boon Feast is a place and a date. The calendar delivers the feast as a scene. A pilgrim crowd has outgrown its ground.

localStateVariants: Out of season the flat is clean with a weir footing.

places.name: The Flu Cordon

why.founding: The Flu began at Stormhold. The north cordoned itself off from its own city. No other line in the province was drawn from the inside out.
why.siteAdvantages: The cordon is a ring drawn at a day's walk from the city. On this side the ring falls on the rim ground. The rim villages never farmed that ground.
why.occupantsMotive: The vicecanons pay a marker-walker to keep the cellar swept. The marker-walker sleeps in the cellar four nights a month.
why.pressures: No record in Stormhold admits that the line was drawn against Stormhold. The ledger of the vicecanons calls the line the northern works.
why.wouldChangeIf: A re-marking of the cordon by the vicecanons would be a diplomatic incident. The markers stand unaltered for that reason.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: uses water as part of the line where it can
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: encircles a plague-abandoned village or a cairn field
hardConstraints: a ring at a day's walk from the city

vibe.silhouette: Marker stones stand at intervals along the line. Their carved faces turn away from the city.
vibe.palette: Lichen grey, marsh green.

vibe.signatureFeature: Every marker faces out from Stormhold. The orientation shows which side the line was meant to hold.

vibe.senses: The site offers wind and the road. Little else is present at this distance from the city.

npcs.note: the marker-walker, present four nights a month

places.name: The Freed Rows

why.founding: The pens emptied and the people in them had nowhere to be. A shelter grew where those people stopped walking.
why.siteAdvantages: The site lies a day south of the pen yard. A column of exhausted people got that far on the first day.
why.occupantsMotive: The shelter persists because people still arrive. The arrivals are now Owing runaways and are no longer freed slaves. The board at the road does not distinguish between them.
why.pressures: The Owing brokers regard the shelter as a receiving house for stolen labour. They say so in Thorn's court.
why.wouldChangeIf: A court order would close the shelter the day the Owing were ruled property. That case is being argued now.

places.name: Gravel Six

why.founding: A second rise lies half a day north of the first hamlet. Overflow from the first hamlet settled it two generations later. The two hamlets are related and competitive. Each thinks that the flood arrangements of the other are inadequate.
why.siteAdvantages: The rise is longer and lower than its neighbour's. That gives more ground and less margin against floods. The founders made that trade knowingly.
why.occupantsMotive: The hamlet's residents live on saltrice from the plain. A ferry-rope crosses the channel. The ferry-rope operators earn only in the wet months, when the hamlet needs it.
why.pressures: In a bad year the rise goes under by a hand's depth. The hamlet then moves bodily to its rival's rise for three weeks. Neither hamlet enjoys the arrangement.
why.wouldChangeIf: The hamlet would abandon the rise after two consecutive bad years. Every household has been counting since the last bad year.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: above the seasonal maximum, beside a channel
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: refuge for its neighbours in flood
hardConstraints: a longer, lower gravel rise on the same plain, not a hill

occupants: D2 hazards from the channel appear in the wet months.

notableNpcSlots.role: ferry-rope keeper who charges by the season

vibe.palette: Saltrice is green in season and silt grey out of season. The post of the ferry rope is tarred black.
vibe.materials: The houses are reed and mud. They use an unusual amount of tarred timber. The timber was salvaged off the channel traffic.

places.name: Guar Ground

why.founding: The site is a second, smaller drying ground on the Thorn side. Dunmer holdings drive their guar here in the dry months. The saltrice ground stands bare in the dry months.
why.siteAdvantages: A shallow basin holds a skin of water two months longer than the plain. Its hard edges hold a herd.
why.occupantsMotive: Two Dunmer holdings and one Argonian village use it in rotation. The Dres set the rotation. No holding has owned the ground since. The rotation still holds.
why.pressures: The guar and the wild herds need the same water in the same weeks. The holdings deal with that by killing whatever else arrives.
why.wouldChangeIf: The rotation would break in the first year that a holding brought more guar than the basin can water. One of the two holdings is visibly building its herd to that size.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: the last water in a drying landscape
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: the region's ecological engine; villages time their year on it
hardConstraints: a basin holding water into the dry season
hard edges to hold a herd
preferences: rotation stakes with three sets of marks
a rope fence taken down in the wet

occupants: D3 predators come for the guar at night.

notableNpcSlots.role: herder who counts in Dunmeris to annoy the village
village elder who holds the third set of marks

vibe.palette: The mud is cracked and pale. The water is brown. The guar hide is grey-green. Dunmer holding banners hang on the stakes in dull red.

places.name: High Wrappings

why.founding: The site is the crown terrace of the second hammock. It is older and smaller than the terrace of the first hammock. Its people will not take charity from the first hammock. Their dead have been up there longer.
why.siteAdvantages: A single enormous trunk has a natural triple fork at fourteen metres. The fork needed almost no building to carry a terrace.
why.occupantsMotive: The village tends the lower wrappings. The last climb past the third fork was two years ago. The trunk above the fork is hollow. A creature dens in the hollow trunk.
why.pressures: The trunk is dying from the top. The terrace is in the dying part. The village keeps that quiet.
why.wouldChangeIf: The terrace would have to come down before the tree does. The village has not begun to plan for it.

sitingPrefs.waterRelation: above the flood, in one great trunk over the village
sitingPrefs.neighbourRelation: one per inhabited hammock; the region's signature sacred form
hardConstraints: a natural high fork over the village
part of Keeps-The-Second-Hammock
preferences: wrappings visibly older than the neighbouring hammock's

notableNpcSlots.role: islander who knows the tree is dying

places.name: Last Landing

why.founding: The north-eastern river is navigable as far as Last Landing. Cargo that goes further inland is carried by porters.
why.siteAdvantages: A rock sill crosses the channel. Deep water lies below the sill. Boulders lie above the sill. The channel has a bank on both sides.
why.occupantsMotive: Last Landing exists to change cargo from hull to back. Every trade at the landing follows from that change of cargo.
why.pressures: The porters and the boat crews price against each other twice a day. They bargain in public and loudly.
why.wouldChangeIf: The landing would move upstream permanently if the sill were blasted. Two generations of residents have proposed blasting the sill.

hardConstraints: a rock sill ending navigation

vibe.palette: The river is green below the sill and white over it. The two halves of the settlement are quite different colours.
vibe.materials: The quay below the sill is stone. Above the sill the settlement is timber and reed.
vibe.signatureFeature: The sill is the signature feature. A person who stands on the sill can touch a laden boat on one side. A laden porter is within reach on the other side.

why.occupantsMotive: Villagers bring their young to the Last Stone Course. A teacher tells them why the province stopped building in stone.
why.pressures: Mazzatun is four days east of the site. Mazzatun is building in stone now. That makes the lesson of the Last Stone Course urgent again.

places.name: Lightning Yard

why.siteAdvantages: The yard stands on a channel bank with running water for flushing. A rock face stands at its back. It is far enough from the first works that the smells stay apart.
why.occupantsMotive: The yard makes lanterns. The luminescent organs keep for a season if handled right. This yard handles them better than the other yard. The brother who runs it regards that as settled proof.
why.pressures: Both yards depend on the same hunters. The hunters play the yards against each other every season. The price of a live wamasu has doubled in five years.
why.wouldChangeIf: The yard would merge with the Charge Works when either brother died. Both families know it.

places.name: Moon Court

why.siteAdvantages: The court stands on a dark upland flat. No light shows within four kilometres. A wall of rock to the north stops the wind without blocking the sky.
why.occupantsMotive: Two alchemists live at the court. Stormhold practitioners book nights there in rotation. They pay for the darkness. One spoiled night voids the booking.
why.pressures: The cutting sheds at Crystalgate have begun to burn lamps late. The northern sky at the court is measurably worse than a decade ago.
why.wouldChangeIf: The court would be worthless if a lit building went up on the ridge. The alchemists have started buying ridge land to prevent it.

hardConstraints: no artificial light within four kilometres
clear sky and a wind break

why.occupantsMotive: Four villages send offerings each wet season, in rotation. A headwoman who is asked why will say it is her turn.
why.pressures: The offerings are increasingly practical. They are tools and salt, not symbols. The older villagers find that embarrassing.
why.wouldChangeIf: The villages would abandon the shelf in a dry decade. They would set it up again after the next bad flood.

why.founding: Salt is the north's second currency. The Tear road stage prefers salt to coin. The delta makes salt for free, given sun and time.
why.siteAdvantages: The site is a flat tidal margin with high evaporation. A rock bar keeps the sea out of the pans except when the families open it to the sea water.
why.occupantsMotive: Six families work the pans. The tide sets the rotation, not agreement. This avoids most quarrels.
why.pressures: The salt smugglers on the rim ledge buy here. The pan families weigh the salt and take the coin.
why.wouldChangeIf: The pans would flood permanently if the rock bar were breached. Traders across the north would feel the loss of the barter economy.

why.pressures: Living in stone is a compromise. The tribe's neighbours notice it. The tribe answers that they did not build it.
why.wouldChangeIf: The hold would be the north's refuge of last resort in a real emergency. The tribe has said as much.

places.name: Thorn

why.founding: Fields ring Thorn, which is a rarity in the north. The fields grow saltrice on temperate grassland. The farmers first grew it for House Dres. They now grow it for whoever holds the title.
why.siteAdvantages: Thorn stands on firm grassland above a delta. The Tear road runs out to Morrowind. River access runs down to the coast. No other place in Argonia has all three together.
why.occupantsMotive: The vicecanon governs Thorn. The field-owners decide in practice. The Dunmer minority holds the trade. The Dunmer remember who used to hold the people.
why.pressures: Every field title is disputed. The smugglers pay the guards, who look away from the smuggling. Both sides of the argument are funded from the border tolls.
why.wouldChangeIf: The people of Thorn would turn on one another if Morrowind pressed a claim. They know it.

why.wouldChangeIf: If a delta shift took the salt gates, the crop would fail in two seasons.

why.wouldChangeIf: The camp would end on the day that the An-Xileel gave a ruling either way. The families fear the ruling more than the wait.

why.founding: Hissmir's Trials cannot admit all of the waiting pilgrims at once. The pilgrims who are not admitted camp on the last dry ground before the village. Some of them camp there for a week. A few stay for a whole season.
why.siteAdvantages: The camp stands on the last firm ground on the pilgrim path. Water and wood are at hand. The village is visible from the camp, two hundred metres off.
why.occupantsMotive: The pilgrims keep an order of arrival. Most of them are Hist-less and unwilling to go home. The Root Stewards do not recognise the order. The pilgrims in the camp obey it anyway.

why.wouldChangeIf: The camp would empty overnight if the Stewards refused a new arrival. The Stewards cannot refuse. For that reason the camp keeps growing.

places.name: Went-Down-Slowly

why.founding: Went-Down-Slowly stands on drying peat beside an upland tarn in the border mountains. Five houses went into the ground over about a decade. The peat beneath them compacted slowly. The households kept re-levelling the floors until the doors would no longer open.
why.siteAdvantages: When the houses were built, this was the best-drained ground in the district. The ground was drying peat, which is why it sank.
why.occupantsMotive: The last household left while the roof was still intact. The walls then stood at an angle of eleven degrees.
why.pressures: The subsidence has not stopped. The site is measurably lower each decade. The hollow now holds water for half the year.
why.wouldChangeIf: The site would be a pond within two generations. The people of the nearby villages have already stopped using its name.

places.name: Wolk Market
sources: uesp:Lore:Ten-Maur-Wolk (the junction and the Imperial renaming; the town is ours)

why.founding: A market grew where the Tear road out of Morrowind meets the marsh tracks and the poled water routes from the north villages. Its name is the name of the ruin off the road to the east, shortened. The local villages did not want a town named after Boethiah. No set of directions worked without the landmark either.
why.siteAdvantages: The market stands on firm ground at the hinge of the three roads. It lies above the flooding that closes the road on either side for two months a year. Spring water suffices for a market. It is not enough to tempt a port builder.
why.occupantsMotive: The market takes a cut of the goods moving between the interior, the border city and the smugglers' port. On every market day, three sets of weights are argued into one here.
why.pressures: The vicecanons want the market fees. The river brokers want the warehousing. The market has spent forty years keeping both out.
why.wouldChangeIf: Armies would fight over the market in the week that any of the three roads mattered militarily. The town has three walls and no fourth.

why.founding: Zuuk was a Kothringi settlement. It died in 2E 561, one year into the Flu. The name of its founder is still on it.
